title: Quiet intrusion and data exfiltration
scenario: A partner organisation has notified you that data belonging to your company appeared on a criminal forum. Nothing has alerted internally. It is 08:30 and you are reviewing the evidence collected overnight. Click each host to read what was found, then answer the questions.

fin2.summary: Regular outbound connections to a domain registered 9 days ago, and a signed Windows binary loading a DLL from a user directory. Antivirus reports the host clean.
lines: EDR   rundll32.exe (signed, Microsoft) loaded C:\Users\jhale\AppData\Roaming\vcx32.dll
EDR   parent process: winword.exe  (document opened 11 days ago)
NET   10.8.4.22 -> cdn-sync-eu[.]net:443  every 60s +/- 4s, 812 bytes avg   (9 days)
NET   domain cdn-sync-eu[.]net registered 9 days ago, no reputation
AV    full scan completed, 0 detections
AUTH  jhale authenticated to FILE-SRV at 02:38 (jhale does not work nights)

exec.summary: The executive's account authenticated from two locations that cannot both be true.
lines: AUTH  m.okafor  VPN login  10:14  source 92.0.2.41   (Dublin)
AUTH  m.okafor  VPN login  10:41  source 203.0.113.77 (Singapore)
AUTH  both sessions active concurrently for 26 minutes
EDR   no malicious process, no unexpected files, scan clean
AUTH  password last changed 7 months ago, no MFA enrolled

dc.summary: A gap in the security log during the incident window, and a scheduled task nobody recognises.
lines: SEC   no security events logged between 02:10 and 02:55 (host was running)
TASK  scheduled task 'WinSysUpd' created 02:31, runs at every boot
TASK  action: powershell -enc <base64>  (decodes to an outbound connection)
AUTH  after the IT team reset jhale's password at 06:00, access resumed at 06:12
EDR   scan clean

file.summary: Large overnight read by a finance account. No malware artefacts on the server itself.
lines: FILE  jhale read 4.2 GB from \\FILE-SRV\finance\ between 02:40 and 03:15
FILE  normal daily volume for this account: under 60 MB
EDR   no unexpected files, no new services, scan clean
SEC   all security events present, no gaps

proxy.summary: A matching outbound upload shortly afterwards.
lines: PROXY 10.8.4.22  POST  https://filetransfer-eu[.]example/upload  4.1 GB  03:22
PROXY category: file sharing   action: ALLOWED (category not blocked)
PROXY no other host uploaded more than 12 MB that night

fin1.summary: Received the same phishing document. It was not opened.
lines: MAIL  message with attachment 'Invoice_Q3.docm' delivered 11 days ago
EDR   attachment never opened, no child processes
EDR   scan clean
MAIL  no matching message delivered
EDR   scan clean, no anomalous network activity

tasks.prompt: Select every host showing evidence that it is itself compromised. Do not select hosts that only recorded the attacker's activity.

Antivirus reports FIN-WS-02 clean, yet a signed Microsoft binary is loading an unknown DLL and beaconing on a fixed interval. Which capability is needed to detect and investigate activity of this kind?

options.label: Update the antivirus definitions and rescan
Endpoint detection and response, using behavioural analysis and a full process timeline
File integrity monitoring on the Windows system directories
A host based firewall blocking outbound connections

tasks.prompt: IT reset the compromised user's password at 06:00 and the attacker regained access at 06:12 using the scheduled task on DC-01. What does that scheduled task represent?

options.label: A trojan
A backdoor providing ongoing unauthorised access
A rootkit
A logic bomb

tasks.prompt: DC-01 logged no security events between 02:10 and 02:55 while it was running. How should this be treated?

options.label: As a benign quiet period, since nothing was happening at that hour
As an indicator of compromise, consistent with the attacker clearing the log
As a false positive produced by the SIEM
As normal log retention trimming old events

tasks.prompt: EXEC-LT itself is clean, but the executive's account authenticated from Dublin and Singapore 27 minutes apart with both sessions active. What is the finding and the correct immediate action?

options.label: Malware on EXEC-LT; reimage the laptop
Impossible travel indicating credential compromise; disable the sessions, reset the credential and enrol MFA
A VPN artefact; no action required
A brute force attempt; enable account lockout

tasks.prompt: Counsel expects litigation and asks you to make sure the relevant mailboxes and file server logs are not removed by the 90 day retention policy. What are they asking for?

options.label: Chain of custody
A legal hold
E-discovery
An attestation

subtasks.label: Identify the compromised hosts
subtasks.correctNote: FIN-WS-02 has the loaded DLL, the beacon and the out of hours authentication. DC-01 has the log gap and an unrecognised persistence mechanism. FILE-SRV and PROXY-01 only recorded the attacker's activity using stolen credentials, and are not themselves compromised. EXEC-LT is clean: the credential was compromised, not the laptop. FIN-WS-01 received the document and never opened it.

subtasks.label: Detection capability required
subtasks.correctNote: A signed Microsoft binary loading a malicious DLL leaves no file signature to match. Behavioural detection with a recorded process timeline is what surfaces it, which is EDR.

subtasks.label: Classify the persistence mechanism
subtasks.correctNote: It gives the attacker a route back in after the credential was reset, which is a backdoor. The macro document was the trojan that let them in originally; those are two different stages.

subtasks.label: Interpret the log gap
subtasks.correctNote: A running system generates security events. A gap is positive evidence that something removed them, which is why logs are forwarded off host in the first place.

subtasks.label: Handle the executive account
subtasks.correctNote: Two concurrent sessions from locations that cannot both be true is impossible travel, and the endpoint is clean. The compromise is the credential: kill the sessions, reset it, and enrol MFA, which is what would have prevented it.

subtasks.label: Respond to counsel
subtasks.correctNote: Suspending routine deletion because litigation is anticipated is a legal hold. Chain of custody would document handling of evidence you have already collected.
